subject: Events & Parallel Scripts
arc_note: Grade 2 · Ontario Math C3 (Coding). This subject's distinct angle is EVENTS — the hat block that TRIGGERS a script (when green flag clicked, when I receive a message) — and PARALLEL SCRIPTS started by events. Builds on the proven two-sprite number-path lane (Bit green bit_wave + Pixel purple pixel_wave on a shared 0–5 clamped path) but the NEW idea is that a script only runs when its EVENT happens: (a) two scripts under the SAME 'when green flag' event run in PARALLEL (concurrent, started together); (b) a script can BROADCAST a message, and a 'when I receive <message>' script starts in response. Loops/variables OUT. ≤8 blocks across the two scripts. Every sheet's question is about the COMBINED outcome AND/OR which event made each script run (matching event→script, predicting, altering the event, debugging a broken event link). solution.py models BOTH scripts as (trigger_event, moves), tracks fired events (green flag + any broadcast), runs only triggered scripts, and asserts both landings + the event behaviour. The event layer (what triggers / in what order / does it run at all) is what distinguishes this subject from Block Coding (Concurrent), where one green flag simply started both. Two mascots = the two sprites/scripts (C4-L3); TG answer key explains the event timing + the common error (thinking a script with no matching event still runs, or that broadcast and receive messages must match). Scaffold introduces the receive/broadcast pair only after the same-event parallel case is understood (C3-L4). Cite Grade-2 C3.1 + C3.2 verbatim ('sequential and concurrent events').
